newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU parliament gives Commission new BSE warning.
newsitem.headline: EU parliament gives Commission new BSE warning.

text.p: More than 100 Euro MPs are expected on Thursday to support a motion demanding the immediate dismissal of European Commission President Jacques Santer and his team of 19 commissioners for mishandling the mad cow crisis.

But parliamentary sources said the censure motion tabled by Belgian Socialist Jose Happart would fall far short of garnering the two-thirds of votes cast and an absolute majority of 314 votes in the assembly needed for it to pass.

Happart says the EU commissioners should be dismissed for failing to give public health priority over economic interests and failing to stand up to British political pressure when deciding how to deal with the spread of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).
He says the Commission also failed to carry out BSE inspections in Britain between 1990-94.
"It will be a further warning to Santer," said one source.

On Wednesday, Euro MPs turned out in force to vote by an overwhelming majority in support of a resolution presented by the mainstream Socialist and Christian Democrat groups giving Santer nine months to put matters right.
Most Euro MPs feel it would be unfair to make Santer and his team, appointed in January 1995, the scapegoat for mistakes made mainly during President Jacques Delors's term of office.

But they endorsed a highly critical report by a special committee of inquiry into the crisis caused by the public health scare caused last March by the announcement that BSE could be transmitted to humans.
The report by a 19-member cross-party committee condemned Britain's failure to enforce BSE controls and the refusal of its Minister of Agriculture to appear before the inquiry.
But the parliament, which has no power to take action against member states, shied away on Wednesday from demanding that the Commission take legal action against Britain.
The report urged the Commission to take corrective measures, notably a shake-up of its food safety and consumer health services.
